==English==
{{wp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|citie|cittie|cyte|cytee||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
{{inh+|en|enm|cite}}, {{der+|en|fro|citet|cite|nocap=1}}, {{der+|en|la-lat|civitas|cīvitātem|city|nocap=1}}, in {{der|en|la-cla|-}} "citizenry", derived from {{m|la|cīvis|t=fellow-citizen}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱey-|t=lie down; settle}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|hīwan|g=p|t=members of one's household, servants}}. See {{m|en|hewe}}. {{doublet|en|civitas}}. Mostly displaced native {{ncog|ang|burg}}, whence {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|borough}}.

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}
[[File:Empire State Building Aerial.JPG|thumb|Part of New York City, a large '''city''' with many tall buildings.]]
[[File:Aerial view of Wells.jpg|thumb|Despite its small size, Wells is a '''city''' because of its cathedral.]]

# {{senseid|en|Q515}}A large [[settlement]], bigger than a [[town]]; sometimes with a specific legal definition, depending on the place.
#: {{ux|en|São Paulo is the largest '''city''' in South America.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 6-3|act=I|scene=i|page=147|column=2|passage=Ah, knovv you not the '''Citie''' fauours them, / And they haue troupes of Souldiers at their beck?}}
#* {{RQ:Ferguson Zollenstein|IV|passage=So this was my future home, I thought!{{...}}Backed by towering hills, the but faintly discernible purple line of the French boundary off to the southwest, a sky of palest Gobelin flecked with fat, fleecy little clouds, it in truth looked a dear little '''city'''; the '''city''' of one's dreams.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-09-07|volume=408|issue=8852|magazine=w:The Economist
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/briefing/21585002-enthusiasts-think-data-services-can-change-cities-century-much-electricity The multiplexed metropolis]
|passage=But clever '''cities''' will not necessarily be better ones.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2014-06-14|volume=411|issue=8891|magazine=w:The Economist
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21604091-it-possible-sniff-out-problems-sewer-pipes-they-happen-its-gas It's a gas]
|passage=One of the hidden glories of Victorian engineering is proper drains. Isolating a '''city'''’s effluent and shipping it away in underground sewers has probably saved more lives than any medical procedure except vaccination.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2020-07-15|author=Mike Brown talks to Paul Clifton|title=Leading London's "hidden heroes"|journal=Rail|page=42|text=All our stations have changed. We have to constrain numbers. We have to mandate face coverings. These are massive changes in what is a public transport '''city'''. This is not a car '''city'''.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|author=Ivana Kottasová|title=‘Kamikaze’ drones are the latest threat for Ukraine. Here’s what we know|magazine=w:CNN|url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/10/17/europe/kamikaze-drones-explained-update-intl|date=2022-10-17|passage=The Ukrainian government says Kyiv, Vinnytsia, Odesa, Zaporizhzhia and other '''cities''' have suffered a barrage of drone attacks, and pleaded with Western countries to step up their assistance in the face of the new challenge. {{...}} But Ukraine claimed its forces had shot down one of these drones for the first time last month near the '''city''' of Kupyansk in Kharkiv.}}
# {{lb|en|UK|historical|_|in|_|Ireland|and|Commonwealth}} A settlement granted special status by royal charter or [[letters patent]]; traditionally, a settlement with a [[cathedral]] regardless of size.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1976|author=Cornelius P. Darcy|title=The Encouragement of the Fine Arts in Lancashire, 1760-1860|publisher=Manchester University Press|isbn=9780719013300|page=20
|passage=Manchester, incorporated in 1838, was made the centre of a bishopric in 1847 and became a '''city''' in 1853. Liverpool was transformed into a '''city''' by Royal Charter when the new diocese of Liverpool was created in 1880.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2014|author=Graham Rutt|title=Cycling Britain's Cathedrals Volume 1|publisher=Lulu.com|isbn=9781326056049|page=307
|passage=St Davids itself is the smallest '''city''' in Great Britain, with a population of less than 2,000.}}
# {{lb|en|Australia}} The [[central business district]]; [[downtown]].
#: {{ux|en|I'm going into the '''city''' today to do some shopping.}}
# {{lb|en|slang}} A large amount of something {{q|used after the noun}}.
#: {{ux|en|It’s video game '''city''' in here!}}
